company_wide_context.notes: CROSS-CUTTING DATA ISSUE — operating_temp_max is overstated on ALL FOUR MiR DB rows. Every MiR specification sheet states the operating ambient range as '5–25°C for continuous use, maximum 40°C for 1 hour' (MiR250 p.11; MiR600 p.9; MiR1350 p.9; MiR1200 Pallet Jack specifications.pdf p.1, printed there as '5–25 | 41–77°F, 40°C | 104°F for up to 1 hour'). The DB stores operating_temp_max=40 for MiR250, MiR600 and MiR1350 — i.e. the ONE-HOUR PEAK, not the sustainable continuous limit. operating_temp_max is a COND_KO field; using the 1-hour peak means a MiR robot would pass a tender requiring sustained 40 °C operation that it cannot actually sustain. This pass recorded 25 (the continuous figure) as the conservative value for all four products and flags the existing 40s for a Tech Lead ruling on which semantics AP0 intends. AP0 ALLOWED-VALUES GAP — ingress_protection_rating cannot express IP21: 'MiR250 Specifications 2.99.pdf' p.1 states 'IP rating  IP21', but AP0's allowed_values for ingress_protection_rating are ['None','IP20','IP44','IP52','IP54','IP65','IP67'] — IP21 is not among them, so the value could not be written at all. The DB currently holds IP20 for MiR250, which is a different (lower) rating, not the datasheet's. NON-CONFORMING VALUES ALREADY IN THE DB (across the MiR rows, not introduced here): top_module_type contains 'Pallet Lift' (MiR250, MiR600, MiR1350) — not in AP0's allowed_values ['None','Lift','Hook','Shelf Carrier','Conveyor','Roller','Cobot arm']; cleanroom_class holds 'ISO 4 (optional)' (MiR250) — allowed_values are only ['None','ISO 1–9']; functional_safety_level holds 'PLd (verify)' (MiR250) — allowed_values are ['None','PLd','PLe','SIL 2','SIL 3']; load_detection holds 'Camera/Vision (AI pallet detection)' (MiR1200) — allowed_values are ['None','Camera/Vision','Laser/LiDAR profiling','RFID','Barcode/DataMatrix','Mechanical/Tactile','Predefined coordinates','Other']. AP0 DATA-TYPE OBSERVATION: drop_accuracy_angle and pick_req_accuracy_angle are Integer ° fields, but every MiR sheet specs sub-degree docking orientation accuracy (±0.5° MiR250, ±0.3° MiR600/MiR1350 at a VL-marker). These values cannot be stored without either rounding to 0 (claiming perfect accuracy) or to 1 (overstating error 2–3×), so this pass left them null. Worth raising as a data-type gap. NOT MAPPABLE — AP0 has no aisle-width field for AMRs: all three of the MiR250/600/1350 sheets devote 4–6 pages to detailed operational corridor widths (e.g. MiR250 p.4 'Operational corridor width  Standard settings: 1.45' / 'MiR250 Dynamic  Standard settings: 1.30 m'; MiR600 p.3 'Standard settings: 1.80 m / Reduced safety settings: 1.20 m'), which is exactly the kind of KO-relevant geometry min_aisle_width captures — but min_aisle_width exists only in 'Logistics:AGV:Forklift' and 'Logistics:AGV:Tugger' scope, not AMR. Same class of gap as the missing Forklift turning-radius field found earlier this session. VDA 5050 is NOT mentioned in ANY of these five files; the DB carries vda5050_compatible=1 on all four rows. Not contradicted (absence ≠ denial per Blank≠Zero), so left null here — but noted, since three of these are full multi-page official spec sheets where one would expect it to appear if claimed.

products.variant_group: The sheet documents TWO configurations throughout its space-requirements section (pp.4–9): 'MiR250' and 'MiR250 Dynamic'. They were NOT split into separate products because every difference between them is an operational-space figure (corridor width, doorway width, pivot width, charging-station clearances) and AP0 has no AMR field to hold any of them — all payload, speed, dimension, battery and environment specs are shared. Flagged in case a reviewer disagrees. An 'ESD version' (different cover colour, ESD certified) and 'cleanroom wheels' are also referenced (p.1, p.2, p.11) as further configurations.

products.notes: CONFLICTS (existing DB values NOT overwritten): (1) ingress_protection_rating DB='IP20' vs datasheet 'IP21' — source: p.1, 'General information' block, row 'IP rating  IP21'. NOTE this is unresolvable as data: IP21 is not in AP0's allowed_values, so the correct value literally cannot be stored (see company_wide_context). (2) charge_time DB=10 min vs datasheet 52 min — source: p.9, 'Charging time from 10%–90% with MiR Charge 48V ... 52 min'. The DB's 10 most likely comes from p.10's opportunity-charging ratio table ('10 min charging: 2 h and 40 min runtime'), which is a charge-to-runtime RATIO entry, not a charge duration — i.e. the DB value appears to answer a different question than the field asks. (3) operating_temp_max DB=40 vs conservative datasheet value 25 — source: p.11 (see company_wide_context; affects all four MiR products). WRONG-SCOPE / WRONG-SEMANTICS TRAP AVOIDED: p.1 prints 'Ground clearance  25–28 mm'. This was deliberately NOT written to min_ground_clearance, whose AP0 hint defines it as the ROBOT HEIGHT needed to drive UNDER a carrier ('Source: vehicle height spec'). The 300 mm 'Height' row was used instead. Writing 25–28 would have understated a KO_IF_LT field by ~10×. FULL DOCKING-ACCURACY MATRIX (pp.2–3, only the VL-marker row was mapped): VL-marker ±3/±3 mm, ±0.5°; V-marker ±9/±17 mm, ±3°; Bar-marker ±18/±4 mm, ±1.5°; L-marker ±6/±3 mm, ±1°; moving to a position (no marker) ±60/±85 mm, ±4°. A reviewer wanting the conservative rather than the best-case figure should use the 'moving to position' row. drop_accuracy_angle left null — ±0.5° cannot be represented in AP0's Integer ° field (see company_wide_context). NOT MAPPED (no AP0 field): weight 94 kg (+21 kg with traction kits); load surface 800×580 mm; drive/caster wheel diameters; product design life '5 years or 20 000 hours'; cover material; maximum noise level 42–54 dBA; minimum distance to achieve maximum speed '9.5 m length × 2 m width' (p.3); minimum size of detectable object 90×90×90 mm (p.3); docking/undocking times (pp.2–3); traversable gap and step tolerance (p.11); floor-to-wheel friction coefficient 0.60–0.80; maximum altitude 2000 m; battery weight/dimensions/voltage/capacity/cycle life (pp.9–10); the entire pp.4–9 operational-space section (no AMR aisle-width field — see company_wide_context). LEFT NULL DELIBERATELY: autonomous_obstacle_bypass — p.12 describes 'Collision avoidance  Triggered by a human or other obstacle in the path of travel' under 'Safety functions', immediately after 'The robot stops if a safety function is triggered', i.e. this is stop-and-wait behaviour, not documented re-routing around an obstacle. The DB carries 1; not contradicted outright, but unsupported by this document. autonomous_charging — the sheet describes docking to a MiR Charge 48V station with CAN-interface charger communication (p.9) and gives docking times, which strongly implies unattended charging, but never states it; DB has 1, left null here. functional_safety_level — '12 safety functions according to ISO 13849-1' (p.12) names the standard but no Performance Level. top_module_type — p.2 says only 'Dimensions for mounting top modules  Equal to robot footprint', without enumerating module types. fleet_management_system / vda5050_compatible / industries_served — not mentioned anywhere in this document.

products.variant_group: MiR600 and MiR1350 share an identical chassis — same length (1350 mm), width (910 mm), height (322 mm), drive/caster wheel diameters, battery, charging options, sensor suite and communication interfaces; they differ only in payload (600 vs 1350 kg), weight (240 vs 244 kg), maximum speed (2.0 vs 1.2 m/s) and maximum slope (3% vs 1%). products.notes: PRODUCT_TYPE CLASSIFICATION QUESTION — FLAGGED, NOT CHANGED (needs a Tech Lead decision): the DB classifies this as 'Mobile AMR' and this pass respected that (existing non-null value, never overwritten) and extracted AMR-scope fields accordingly. But the classification is genuinely arguable. FOR Mobile AMR: both documents call it an 'Autonomous mobile robot (AMR)' verbatim (specifications p.1 'Designated use'), MiR's whole range is AMRs, and the DB already types the 1350 kg MiR1350 as Mobile AMR. FOR Forklift AGV: it has physical FORKS with a 1 140 mm lifting height (specifications p.1), a 2 120 mm mast height, a 750 kg dead weight, 1200 kg payload, and the one-pager positions it explicitly as a forklift replacement ('Replaces forklifts with certified, safe autonomous operation', p.1) doing 'fully automated pallet and rack handling'; config/vehicle_types.json's own llm_guide says Mobile AMR is 'ONLY ... for LIGHT payloads (typically <1000 kg). If payload >1000 kg or if the task is heavy pallet transport → use Forklift AGV instead.' product_type is a hard K.O. (Forklift AGV never matches Mobile AMR), so this is consequential either way. The practical symptom of the unresolved classification is already visible in the DB row, which mixes scopes (see below). CONFLICT (existing DB value NOT overwritten): lift_height DB=200 mm vs datasheet 1 140 mm — source: 'MiR1200 Pallet Jack specifications.pdf' p.1, row 'Maximum fork lifting height  1 140 mm | 44.9 in'. A 200 mm value would describe an under-ride lift, not a pallet-jack mast; this looks like a value carried over from a different MiR product class. Note lift_height is KO_IF_LT, so a 200 mm figure would wrongly disqualify this robot from any tender needing rack-level placement. DOCUMENT SELF-CONTRADICTION BETWEEN THE PAIR: 'mir_palletjack_1_pager.pdf' p.2 prints 'Max. Lift Height: 1120mm' while 'MiR1200 Pallet Jack specifications.pdf' p.1 prints '1 140 mm | 44.9 in'. The specification file is preferred because its imperial conversion corroborates the metric figure (1140 mm = 44.88 in ≈ 44.9 in) whereas 1120 mm would be 44.09 in — i.e. the one-pager's number fails the internal-consistency test the spec sheet passes. Flagged rather than silently reconciled. SOURCE TYPO IN THE ONE-PAGER (do not use): 'mir_palletjack_1_pager.pdf' p.2 states dimensions as 'W=820cm L=1934cm H=2120cm' — these are millimetres mislabelled as centimetres (a 19.3 m long pallet jack is absurd, and the spec file gives the identical numbers in mm). The mm figures from the spec file were used. FURTHER INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES in 'MiR1200 Pallet Jack specifications.pdf' p.1 (metric is consistent, imperial is not): the header banner gives 'Width: 820 mm | 32.28 in' while the Dimensions table gives '820 mm | 31.5 in' (820 mm = 32.28 in, so the table's imperial figure is wrong); the header gives 'Height: 2 120 mm | 83.46 in' while the table gives '2 120 mm | 83.86 in' (2120 mm = 83.46 in, so the table's imperial figure is wrong again). Metric values were used throughout; no AP0 value is affected. NOT MAPPED — height: the 2 120 mm overall height was deliberately NOT written to min_ground_clearance. Unlike the other three MiR models, this is a masted pallet jack, not an under-ride robot, so the AP0 hint's 'robot height / clearance needed to drive UNDER the carrier' semantics simply do not apply. SCOPE BUG IN EXISTING DB ROW (pre-existing): the row is product_type='Mobile AMR' but carries vna_capable, stacking_capability and load_detection — all three exist only in scope 'Logistics:AGV:Forklift'. (load_detection is additionally stored as the non-conforming string 'Camera/Vision (AI pallet detection)'.) This is the DB itself hedging the classification question above. This pass wrote none of them; note that the document DOES strongly support camera/vision-based load detection ('5 pcs 3D cameras, for pallet and obstacle detection', spec p.1; 'ML-based perception: enables shrink-wrapped pallet recognition and rapid, precise, and reliable pallet detection', one-pager p.2; '1 pcs ultrasonic sensor, for detecting pallets are securely placed on the forks', spec p.1) — so if the Tech Lead reclassifies this product as a Forklift AGV, load_detection=['Camera/Vision'] is well evidenced and should be filled then. NOT MAPPED (no AP0 field): weight 750 kg; overall height 2 120 mm; 'Charging Ratio 1:14' (one-pager p.2); 'load-jam detection' (one-pager p.2); the AI/ML perception claims. LEFT NULL DELIBERATELY: load_type — the DB has 'Pallet EUR' but neither document names a pallet standard, only 'pallet and rack handling'. multi_fleet_capable — the one-pager p.2 says the robot 'seamlessly integrates with MFE alongside other MiR robots', which is same-vendor fleet integration, NOT the multi-vendor interoperability this field means. navigation_type — 'advanced navigation algorithms' (one-pager p.1) names no technology. vda5050_compatible — never mentioned; DB has 1. autonomous_obstacle_bypass — DB has 1; the documents describe detection and safe stopping, not documented re-routing.
